description.p: Network Manager is a Linux-native system and network profile manager inspired by NetSetMan Pro, redesigned for Linux best practices.

ul.li: Create unlimited network and system profiles
Switch configurations manually, automatically, or via CLI
Manage IP addresses, DNS, routes, VPN, Wi-Fi profiles
Configure system settings: hostname, proxy, firewall, printer
Auto-switch profiles based on conditions (SSID, gateway, time)

description.p: The application follows GNOME Human Interface Guidelines and uses NetworkManager with your desktop's normal authorization prompts.

screenshot.caption: Network Manager dashboard and feature overview

description.p: First release, made for Fedora with the GNOME desktop:

ul.li: Save network and system settings as profiles and switch between them in one click
Network settings: IP addresses, DNS, routes, Wi-Fi and VPN connections
System settings: hostname, proxy, firewall zone, default printer and timezone
Automatic switching based on the Wi-Fi network, the router or the time of day
Scheduled profile activation and a connection watchdog
Scripts before and after a profile is applied, optionally sandboxed
Optional profile encryption with a passphrase
System tray icon for quick profile switching
Dashboard with live network status and activity
